findings.title: Unverified constraint resolution unlocks daily work including PERMIT/INSPECTION gates
findings.description: LookAheadScheduler.update_constraint() accepts any ConstraintStatus, including RESOLVED, with only free-text notes and no evidence, dual control, or role check. ConstraintType includes PERMIT and INSPECTION. analyze_make_ready() treats non-RESOLVED constraints as the only make-ready blockers (alongside predecessors). generate_daily_plan() schedules only activities with can_start=True. A responsible-party subcontractor or field user who can call update_constraint can mark permit/inspection/safety constraints resolved without obtaining them, causing unpermitted/uninspected work to appear on the daily coordination plan that operators implement as written.
findings.impact: Live work proceeds without required permits or inspections (excavation, hot work, structural hold points), creating utility-strike / collapse / OSHA willful-violation and fatality risk, plus fraudulent look-ahead PPC records.
attack_path: Operator deploys LookAheadScheduler with multi-party constraint workflow (responsible_party set on constraints).
Activity A100 has ConstraintType.PERMIT (or INSPECTION) OPEN, needed_by this week.
analyze_make_ready marks A100 not_ready; generate_daily_plan excludes it.
Attacker (subcontractor / field coordinator named as responsible_party) calls update_constraint(constraint_id, ConstraintStatus.RESOLVED, notes='obtained').
No permit document, inspector sign-off, or second actor required.
analyze_make_ready sets can_start=True; generate_daily_plan includes the activity and crews mobilize.
evidence: update_constraint sets status=RESOLVED and resolved_date with no verification (lines ~178-191).
ConstraintType includes PERMIT and INSPECTION (lines ~46-55).
analyze_make_ready: open_constraints = status != RESOLVED; else can_start=True (lines ~199-218).
generate_daily_plan filters act.can_start (lines ~258-265).
findings.why_not_duplicate: Distinct from permit-tracking/compliance-tracker status forge: this is the look-ahead make-ready/daily-plan gate that commits crews to live work. Not the same as schedule-delay claims classification.

findings.title: Predecessors outside look-ahead window are treated as complete (all([])=True)
findings.description: analyze_make_ready only evaluates predecessors that exist in self.activities. import_from_master only imports activities overlapping the look-ahead window. For any predecessor outside that window, the comprehension yields an empty sequence and Python all([]) is True, so predecessor gates are vacuously satisfied. A PM under liquidated-damages pressure (or any actor controlling import) can produce Ready daily plans for work whose structural/MEP predecessors are incomplete or simply not imported.
findings.impact: Crews start successor work (e.g., finishes before fireproofing, steel before foundation acceptance) based on a false Ready signal → rework, structural/safety failures, and hidden delay exposure.
attack_path: Master schedule: B depends on A; A is delayed/incomplete with planned finish before look-ahead start (or omitted from import).
import_from_master(look_ahead_weeks=2) imports B but not A.
analyze_make_ready for B: predecessors filtered with `if p in self.activities` → empty; all([]) → pred_complete True.
With no open constraints, B.can_start=True and appears on generate_daily_plan.
evidence: pred_complete = all(... for p in act.predecessors if p in self.activities) (lines ~201-204).
import window filter: start <= look_ahead_end and finish >= look_ahead_start (lines ~137-138).
Validated: all([]) is True; activity with missing predecessor marked predecessor-complete.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not previously reported for look-ahead-scheduler. Different root cause from constraint forge (vacuous predecessor check vs status write).

findings.title: Capacity availability uses max overlapping quantity, not sum — enables overbooking shared equipment/crews
findings.description: _get_availability() computes allocated capacity as max(quantity) across overlapping allocations instead of summing concurrent demand. Multiple partial allocations that individually fit can sum above resource.capacity. allocate() and auto_allocate() both trust this check. AllocationStatus.MAINTENANCE is never applied as a hard gate. allocate() also skips the skill matching that find_available_resources() enforces.
findings.impact: Shared tower cranes, excavator fleets, or specialty crews are double-booked across projects → lift conflicts, idle crews waiting on phantom equipment, schedule collapse, and liquidated damages; unskilled allocation via allocate() bypass raises injury risk on welding/structural work.
attack_path: Shared Excavator Fleet capacity=3.
Project A allocate(qty=2) for overlapping window → available becomes 3-max(2)=1.
Project B allocate(qty=1) → OK; availability still computed as 3-max(2,1)=1.
Project C allocate(qty=1) → OK because check still sees available=1.
Total concurrent demand 4 > capacity 3; planner/report shows allocations as successful.
Optional: call allocate() directly for welding request onto crew lacking skills (find_available would have filtered).
evidence: _get_availability: `allocated = max(allocated, alloc.quantity)` (lines ~206-215).
allocate() raises only if available < quantity using that function (lines ~231-237).
auto_allocate → allocate (lines ~254-286).
Validated script: after qty 2+1 overlapping on cap 3, availability still 1; third qty 1 accepted; total 4>3.
allocate() does not re-check required_skills (unlike find_available_resources lines ~185-187).
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not the same as labor-allocation unbounded hours or resource-allocation-optimizer leveling. This is a concrete arithmetic bug in shared-pool capacity that falsely authorizes over-allocation. User asked whether resource-allocation was 'similar?' — this pool optimizer flaw is distinct.

findings.title: assign_worker ignores TERMINATED/SICK/ON_LEAVE and only soft-warns on conflicts
findings.description: WorkerStatus includes ON_LEAVE, SICK, and TERMINATED, and get_workers_by_trade filters to AVAILABLE/ASSIGNED only, but assign_worker() never checks worker.status before creating an Assignment. Conflicting overlapping assignments only print a Warning and still append. Successful assign overwrites status to ASSIGNED, reactivating terminated/leave workers on the roster used by get_daily_roster.
findings.impact: Ghost/terminated workers billed on live activities (payroll/prevailing-wage fraud); sick or leave workers placed on hazardous site work; double-booked workers on concurrent activities → fatigue and missed coverage on safety-critical tasks. Distinct from previously reported unbounded hours_per_day.
attack_path: GC marks worker W as TERMINATED or SICK in the shared LaborAllocation pool.
Subcontractor/superintendent who can call assign_worker(W, activity, ...) still succeeds (only existence check).
worker.status forced to ASSIGNED; get_daily_roster lists them for the activity.
Optionally assign same worker to two overlapping activities — conflicts warned but both kept.
evidence: assign_worker: only `if worker_id not in self.workers: return None` then creates Assignment (lines ~136-160).
Conflicts: print Warning then still append (lines ~142-157).
worker.status = WorkerStatus.ASSIGNED overwrites TERMINATED/SICK/ON_LEAVE (line ~158).
get_workers_by_trade correctly excludes leave/sick/terminated (lines ~198-203) — inconsistent gate.
certifications field never consulted on assign.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior labor-allocation finding was unbounded hours_per_day (MEDIUM). This is a separate dead status/conflict interlock with payroll fraud and unfit-for-duty impact.

findings.title: Toolbox talk attendance is attacker-supplied with no verification — OSHA training record fraud
findings.description: record_talk() accepts an arbitrary attendees list and persists TalkRecord used by get_attendance_summary() for compliance metrics. There is no signature capture, badge/RFID check, acknowledgment, or presenter/attendee separation. A foreman can record talks that never happened or pad attendance for workers who were absent.
findings.impact: Falsified OSHA/site-safety training records for audits and insurance; untrained workers appear trained and are assigned to high-hazard tasks → elevated injury/fatality and willful citation exposure.
attack_path: Foreman generates or selects a toolbox talk id.
Calls record_talk(talk_id, ..., attendees=[entire crew roster]) without conducting the talk or with missing workers.
get_attendance_summary reports total_talks / unique_workers as compliant.
Records produced for auditor/insurance as proof of daily safety training.
evidence: record_talk builds TalkRecord from caller-supplied attendees with no validation (lines ~435-458).
get_attendance_summary aggregates len(r.attendees) and unique names from those records (lines ~460-485).
No attestation, signature, or dual-control fields on TalkRecord.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not in prior reported set (safety-inspection Pass forge, incident CA self-complete, compliance/permit). New surface: training attendance fraud.
